title: Grade 4 Science — Thu, May 21
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 4 of 5: Food preservation and food safety
subject: science

questions.question: Why does food go bad (spoil)?
options: Because microorganisms (bacteria, fungi) grow on it and decompose it
Because we don't eat it fast enough
questions.explanation: Bacteria, fungi, and moulds grow on food and decompose it. Heat, moisture, and time accelerate spoilage.

questions.question: Keeping food in a refrigerator preserves it because:
options: Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
questions.explanation: Refrigeration slows microbial growth — bacteria and fungi grow much slower at low temperatures.

questions.question: Adding salt or sugar to food preserves it because:
options: Salt/sugar draw water out of microorganisms, killing them (osmosis)
questions.explanation: High salt or sugar concentration draws water out of bacteria through osmosis, stopping their growth. This is why pickles and jams last long.

questions.question: Boiling milk before drinking is important because:
options: It kills harmful bacteria and microorganisms
questions.explanation: Boiling kills bacteria (including dangerous pathogens) in raw milk. Always boil milk before drinking unless it is pasteurised.

questions.question: Pickles last for months because of:
options: The oil, salt, and vinegar that prevent microbial growth
questions.explanation: Pickles use salt, oil, vinegar, and spices — all of which inhibit bacterial growth and preserve food.

questions.question: Which method is used to preserve milk for long life (packaged milk)?
questions.explanation: Pasteurisation heats milk to ~72°C for 15 seconds, then rapidly cools it — kills most bacteria without destroying nutrients.

questions.question: Drying fruits (like raisins, figs) preserves them because:
questions.explanation: Microorganisms need water to grow. Drying removes moisture, making the food inhospitable for bacteria and fungi.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe food practice?
options: Keeping cooked and raw food separate
Leaving cooked food uncovered for hours in hot weather
questions.explanation: Leaving cooked food uncovered in hot weather allows rapid bacterial growth. This can cause food poisoning.

questions.question: What is the danger of eating food that has visible mould?
options: Moulds can produce toxins harmful to health
questions.explanation: Mouldy food can contain mycotoxins — toxic substances that can cause food poisoning, liver damage, or illness.

questions.question: Canning preserves food because:
options: Food is heated to kill bacteria and sealed airtight — preventing new contamination
questions.explanation: Canning: food is sterilised (heated), sealed in airtight cans. No oxygen = microorganisms can't grow.

questions.question: Why should you wash fruits and vegetables before eating?
options: To remove pesticides, dirt, and surface bacteria
questions.explanation: Washing removes pesticide residues, soil, and bacteria/parasites that may be on the surface.

questions.question: Jams and jellies last long because of high ___ content.
questions.explanation: High sugar concentration in jams/jellies inhibits microbial growth through osmosis — the same principle as pickling with salt.

questions.question: Which preservation method keeps all nutrients best?
questions.explanation: Freezing preserves food with minimal nutrient loss. Long boiling destroys heat-sensitive vitamins (like Vitamin C).

questions.question: Food poisoning symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea. This is caused by:
options: Bacteria or toxins in spoiled food entering the body
questions.explanation: Food poisoning is caused by eating food contaminated with bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli) or their toxins.

questions.question: Which food needs NO preservation and can be eaten directly?
options: Fresh fruit just plucked from the tree
Opened canned food left for a week
questions.explanation: Fresh fruit directly from the tree is safe and nutritious. The others require proper storage or cooking.
